title: ImageNet: The Dataset That Sparked Deep Learning
hook: A hand-labeled hoard of millions of images turned into the contest that, in 2012, lit the fuse on the deep learning era.
key_points: ImageNet holds millions of images organized into thousands of categories, labeled by hand.
Its labels follow the WordNet hierarchy, giving categories a structured taxonomy.
The ILSVRC challenge ran a classification competition on a subset of ImageNet.
AlexNet's 2012 win on ILSVRC, by a wide margin, kicked off the deep-learning boom.
content_html: ImageNet, built by Fei-Fei Li and collaborators, is a massive collection of hand-labeled images spanning thousands of object categories. The annual ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge (ILSVRC) ran on a subset of it, and when a deep convolutional network called AlexNet won that competition in 2012, it convinced the field that deep learning was the way forward.
extra_html:
How it works

The dataset was assembled by collecting web images and labeling them through large-scale crowdsourcing, with categories drawn from the WordNet hierarchy of concepts. That scale — millions of carefully labeled examples — is what made it possible to train large image models that actually generalized, rather than overfitting a tiny dataset.

Why it matters

Before ImageNet, vision models trained on small datasets and progress was slow. The combination of a huge labeled benchmark and a public competition gave researchers a common yardstick and a reason to push. AlexNet's dramatic ILSVRC win showed that deep neural networks plus lots of data plus GPUs beat hand-engineered features, and the modern era of deep learning followed.

related.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep CNNs (AlexNet)
related.hook: In 2012 a single deep CNN trained on two GPUs crushed the ImageNet contest by a wide margin — and kicked off the deep learning era.

related.title: Deep Residual Learning (ResNet)
related.hook: Stacking more layers used to make networks worse, not better. ResNet's fix — let each layer learn a tweak to its input — unlocked nets over 100 layers deep.
